QUOTE: It then calls `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free` with its own `buffer_alloc_calloc` / `buffer_alloc_free`, or the `_mutexed` variants when `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` is on.
VERDICT: MISS
WHY: The answer says the buffer allocator calls the setter from its init function, but it never says it is the only in-tree user. It also says the setter is "the same hook the library's own allocator uses", which doesn't claim exclusivity.
